questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce your chances of an accident by:

options.text: Not using turn signals so you don't distract other drivers.
Making sure other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: To avoid accidents, be visible to other drivers, use turn signals clearly, keep safe distance, watch ahead, and spot hazards early. Always be ready to react to danger.

questions.question: Unlike other drinks, alcohol:

options.text: Goes into your bloodstream right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goes into your bloodstream right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need digestion. It goes directly through the stomach and small intestine walls into the bloodstream and quickly reaches the brain.

questions.question: No matter what helmet style you choose, you get the most protection when your helmet:
questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Your helmet gives the best protection when it meets DOT and state safety standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, you need to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a higher gear.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: When wearing a protective jacket, it should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you and keep you comfortable. Jackets and pants should be snug enough to not flap in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: When someone tailgates you, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in emergencies.
Should be used together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster it leaves your body.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the faster alcohol builds up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol will still be in your system.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time will remove alcohol from your body. Nothing else can speed up this process.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: May be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have passenger footrests. This prevents your passenger from falling and pulling you off too.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it difficult for drivers to see a motorcycle's turn signals, the rider should:

options.text: Continue to use the mechanical turn signals.
Honk their horn to inform other drivers of any upcoming turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use hand signals.
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to let other drivers know your next move.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Not make sudden movements, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make sudden movements, if possible.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake smoothly when riding on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: There may be less traction available for braking when:

options.text: A motorcycle is straight up and down.
A motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is leaning.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle is leaning, such as in a turn, there is less grip for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stare straight in front of their motorcycle.
Be unwilling to move to avoid a potential hazard.
Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds on the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds on the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds to reduce crash risk. Looking ahead gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, it is important to:

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Know what's happening both in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what's happening both in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: Pay attention to what is ahead of you most. But you also need to know what is behind you. Check your mirrors often to stay aware.

questions.question: When riding in a group, mirrors:

options.text: Should be checked frequently by all riders.
Should be used only by the lead rider.
Should not be checked frequently because they can be a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked frequently by all riders.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, check your mirrors often. This helps you watch the riders behind you and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of a head or neck injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: By wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always possible when riding a motorcycle, no matter your speed. A properly fitted quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of these injuries.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what should happen if you arrive at the same time as another vehicle?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
You should continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an unmarked intersection with no traffic lights at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What should a good lane position do?

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It also keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other riders from sharing your lane and give you room to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcyclists?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots.
questions.explanation: Leather boots offer the best foot protection when riding. They should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, they have blind spots just like cars.
No, because motorcycles are smaller than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they have blind spots just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
